items.body:
All you need is love and connected teams: presenting last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail systems deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including Tapestry, Catalyst Brands, Costco Wholesale, Amazon, Tesco, Uber Eats, The Entertainer, REWE, Westfield, Søstrene Grene, Kwik Fill, M&S, and Nobody's Child.
Kwik Fill
Kwik Fill, a 300+ location convenience chain in the USA, has selected PAR Retail as a technology partner to power its new loyalty programme.
“As we evaluated potential partners, PAR Retail stood apart through its vision for the future of convenience retail and its ability to combine guest engagement with actionable AI driven insights,” says Roy Williams, Senior Vice President Marketing at United Refining Company, parent company of Kwik Fill.
“PAR Intelligence was a significant differentiator for our team. We see tremendous opportunity to leverage the platform as we continue enhancing the experiences we deliver to our guests.”
“The convenience retail industry is at an inflection point. More software isn't the answer. Smarter software is," says Savneet Singh, CEO at PAR Technology. “Kwik Fill gets that. They're building their loyalty programme from scratch on PAR Retail, which means every guest relationship and every data point is theirs from day one. PAR Intelligence makes sure they can act on it. That's the difference between a platform that informs and one that drives outcomes.”
The Beatles Story
The Beatles Story tourist attraction in Liverpool has turned to technology normally associated with the retail sector to help keep its teams connected.
Situated at Liverpool’s Royal Albert Dock, it has introduced a wireless headset system, enabling around 30 employees working across admissions, exhibitions, the Fab4 Store, cafés and guest services to communicate with eachother hands free. The move is designed to help staff respond more quickly to visitor requests and coordinate activity across the attraction without having to leave their work areas or interrupt their interactions with guests.
Andy Kelly, Guest Experience Manager at The Beatles Story, says: “The headsets by Quail Digital have changed the way teams, which previously used an outdated radio system, communicate across the attraction. Introducing the Quail Digital headset system was an important step forward in how we support our teams and serve our guests.”
“Clear, fast communication is essential in a dynamic attraction like ours. We have colleagues working across a number of different areas, and the ability to communicate immediately means we can respond to guest needs more quickly and coordinate support without colleagues having to leave their positions.”
“Just as importantly, it supports our colleagues by making their roles more efficient and connected. We’re constantly looking at ways to improve how we work behind the scenes so that the visitor experience remains seamless. The investment in communication technology is part of that.”
Søstrene Grene
Danish retailer Søstrene Grene has invested DKK 380 million in an automated logistics setup in Denmark and the Netherlands, alongside an implementation of SAP technology.
In a LinkedIn post, the retailer said: “Recently, we welcomed Danish business newspaper Børsen to our distribution centre in Aarslev for a closer look at how automation is helping us build for the future. Importantly, automation is not about replacing our employees. They are being trained to take on more specialised tasks, while automation primarily reduces our reliance on seasonal workers during peak periods and creates a safer working environment with less heavy lifting.”
It added: “The automated journey begins as soon as goods arrive at our distribution centre, where an inbound robotic solution receives and sorts them. In our e-commerce operation, mobile robots pick online orders before automated packing solutions prepare them for shipment. This not only makes our operation more efficient but also reduces the amount of packaging and empty space in each box.”
It concluded: “Automation is helping us increase efficiency, reduce CO₂ emissions across our logistics operations and create a better working environment for our employees - with fewer manual tasks and less heavy lifting. With this strong foundation, we are ready to pursue our ambition of reaching 500 stores across markets in the next few years.”
Puresport
Visualsoft reports a partnership with performance wellness brand Puresport, using Shopify POS to power a charity pop-up. Working alongside the Puresport team, it designed and implemented a complete Shopify POS setup ahead of the “Thrift it back” event to raise money for Greenhouse Sports.
This included configuring the PoS environment, synchronising products and inventory with Shopify, enabling Tap to Pay on staff mobile devices and providing training so the team could confidently process transactions throughout the day.
The project also required overcoming a significant operational challenge. With unreliable Wi-Fi across the venue, there was a risk of payment failures and disruption during the event. Visualsoft assessed the site's connectivity ahead of time and recommended improvements to ensure transactions could be processed consistently.
By connecting every sale directly into Shopify, Puresport was able to track sales and fundraising in real-time while eliminating the manual reconciliation often associated with temporary retail events. Customer, payment and inventory data remained connected throughout the activation, providing complete visibility from a single platform.
Antony Hoyland, Director of Sales at Visualsoft, says: "Temporary retail often creates permanent headaches. Brands can find themselves juggling disconnected payment systems, manual stock updates and unreliable connectivity, all of which impact the customer experience. Our aim was to make the technology invisible; consumers don’t want to know it’s there, and shop staff need it to be out of the way. Puresport's team could focus on talking to customers and supporting a fantastic cause, while Shopify POS handled payments, inventory and reporting behind the scenes."
Tapestry
Tapestry is bringing Coach and Kate Spade into Google's AI shopping ecosystem, making products purchasable directly from Google Search, including AI Mode, and the Gemini app. Now, when shoppers discover a Coach or Kate Spade item while using Gemini or AI Mode, a "Buy" button appears inline. After selecting their product, customers can complete checkout in just a few taps using Google Pay. This eliminates the need for website redirects.
"Consumer behaviours are always evolving. At one time, discovery happened in a store window or a magazine. Then, it happened on social media. Now it's happening inside a conversation with AI," says Joanne Crevoiserat, Chief Executive Officer at Tapestry. "Our goal is for shoppers to find and engage with our brands at the moment when inspiration strikes, whether it be when a consumer passes by one of our stores, peruses our websites, or chats with AI.”
Tapestry has implemented the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), an open industry standard for agentic commerce backed by several tech and e-commerce companies.
"We built this layer to work with our existing operations today, but it's truly protocol agnostic, so we can quickly move into new AI environments as consumer behaviours evolve," says Yang Lu, Chief Information and Digital Officer at Tapestry. "That's possible because of the strategic investments we've made in technology capabilities and infrastructure as well as the strength of our data and consumer insights engine."
UCP powered checkout is now live in the US,, with plans to expand across geographies in the future.
Catalyst Brands
WorkJam, a frontline operations platform, is expanding its partnership with department store JCPenney, part of the Catalyst Brands portfolio.
This covers every brand in the Catalyst portfolio group, including Aéropostale, Brooks Brothers, Lucky Brand, and Nautica, and brings WorkJam's platform to approximately 70,000 associates across North America.
"Serving millions of customers across our unmatched portfolio of iconic brands depends on creating a workforce that is connected, agile, and increasingly AI enabled,” says Andre Joyner, EVP and Chief Human Resources Officer at Catalyst Brands. "We believe the future of work will be defined by how thoughtfully organisations use technology to help associates perform at their best.”
“Through our partnership with WorkJam, we're embedding AI directly into the flow of work, giving associates faster access to needed information, reducing everyday friction, and creating more capacity for managers to lead their teams and serve customers. This expansion reflects our commitment to enabling our talented workforce while deploying AI responsibly and at scale, with the associate experience at the centre of everything we do."
Flipdish
Flipdish, an AI platform for restaurants, reports that independent restaurants throughout the UK and Ireland have placed over 10,000 orders via its AI Phone Agent, resulting in revenues in excess of £230,000.
Initially launched at Dished Live 25 in November, the product (which has helped to facilitate over 13,000 orders to date), was created in response to a common problem restaurants face: phone orders are still an important source of income, but calls are often missed during peak times, meaning potential orders are abandoned.
The AI Phone Agent answers incoming calls, takes orders, suggests appropriate add-on products such as side dishes, and submits the confirmed order right to the Flipdish PoS, KDS or terminal, allowing the operator to receive orders without removing its staff from food preparations and serving customers in-store.
"10,000+ orders and £230k in revenue is a great milestone, but the real win is what it represents. Fewer missed calls, less chaos during peak service, and more orders captured without dragging staff away from the kitchen or the counter,” says Conor McCarthy, Co-Founder and CEO at Flipdish. "Restaurants shouldn't have to choose between answering the phone and looking after the customers in front of them. We built AI Phone Agent to take that pressure off teams. It can take multiple calls and orders at the same time, so revenue keeps coming in even when the restaurant is flat out."
The Entertainer
UK toy retailer, The Entertainer, has appointed THG Commerce, part of THG Ingenuity, as its new digital commerce partner. The multi-year tie up will see THG Commerce design, build and power The Entertainer’s next-generation digital experience, with the aim of creating a more intuitive, inspiring and personalised journey for families, gift buyers and adult toy and collectible enthusiasts.
THG Commerce will deploy AI enabled shopping assistance, conversational discovery and intent led search capabilities to help customers explore thousands of products and find the right choice more intuitively. These capabilities draw on the wider THG Ingenuity collaboration with Google Cloud, which harnesses Vertex AI Commerce Search and Gemini.
Alongside smarter search and discovery, the new experience will bring together richer content, curated product journeys and personalised recommendations to inspire customers throughout the purchasing journey. THG Commerce will deliver a new web and mobile experience, together with an enhanced Click & Collect journey designed to create a more seamless connection between digital discovery and The Entertainer’s nationwide store network.
The new platform is expected to launch in spring 2027 and has been designed to provide a foundation for future opportunities across loyalty, retail media and social commerce as The Entertainer continues to develop its omnichannel customer proposition.
Guess
GXO Logistics and Exotec have deployed Exotec’s Skypod system at GXO's Venlo, Netherlands, facility, home to fashion brand Guess. The installation includes 127 Skypod robots, 60,000 rack locations, eight goods-to-person picking stations and 200 metres of conveyor network. The system is also capable of processing up to 70,000 pieces per day, achieving throughput of up to 2,200 order lines per hour during peak periods.
With the deployment of the automated solution, GXO says it is enhancing fulfilment operations for Guess across EMEA and Asia by increasing throughput, improving productivity and supporting future growth.
Mark Donné, Operations Manager, GXO Venlo, says: "The impact has been evident from day one. Our automated solution with Exotec, tailored specifically for Guess, has helped take our operation to the next level, enabling faster processing, greater predictability and a smoother workflow across the site. As our business with Guess continues to grow, we have the scalability and flexibility needed to support future demand."
Wim Vermeir, Senior Sales Executive Benelux, Exotec, comments: "Fashion logistics doesn't tolerate approximation - high SKU counts, seasonal spikes, and EMEA wide distribution require precision engineering, not off-the-shelf automation. With GXO, we designed a system built specifically for those demands, and the throughput numbers speak for themselves. The result is a highly efficient operation that supports both current performance and future growth."
Westfield
Westfield Rise, Westfield's in-house retail media agency, has launched new audience measurement capabilities across Westfield London and Westfield Stratford City, with the aim of giving advertisers deeper insight into how campaigns influence attention, engagement and store visitation.
The launch is backed by data which found that shoppers exposed to advertising were 27% more likely to visit a brand's store than those who weren't exposed to a campaign. Additional findings include: experiential activations delivered an average dwell time of 1 minute and 28 seconds; nearly one in four visitors engaged with an activation for more than 60 seconds.
Developed in partnership with Digeiz, the measurement solution uses AI powered technology to analyse visitor journeys across shopping centres. The UK launch forms part of a wider roll-out of Westfield Rise’s audience measurement platform across 23 Westfield destinations in Europe.
REWE
REWE, a supermarket chain in Germany and the main brand of REWE Group, has announced a partnership with Uber Eats. In a LinkedIn post, Moritz Bernhard, GM Grocery & Retail - Central & Eastern Europe at Uber, said: “A big milestone for our grocery and retail business in Germany.”
He added: “I’m excited to share that we are launching a new partnership with REWE on Uber Eats. Starting this week in Frankfurt, users will have access to a broad selection of REWE products through the Uber and Uber Eats app. And we have big plans ahead: over the coming months, we’re bringing 60-minute grocery delivery to more than 100 cities across the country.”
He concluded: “A special thank you to E-commerce Director Clemens Uwe Bauer and the entire REWE team for the trust and great collaboration, and to everyone at Uber who worked hard to bring this partnership to life.”
REWE has also gone live with Wolt in Cologne and Just Eat in Hamburg and Jena.
Waitrose
Waitrose has extended its partnership with Trust Retail, a Trust Payments business, for a further five years, taking the relationship through to November 2031 as the supermarket prepares to accelerate the roll-out of Trust Retail’s inventory management technology across its store estate.
The technology was first trialled in a Waitrose store in March 2026 and is now live across eight stores. A wider roll-out is scheduled to begin at the end of September, with approximately 125 stores expected to be live before Christmas and the remaining Waitrose estate scheduled to follow by March 2027.
Trust Retail’s inventory management technology gives Waitrose partners a real-time view of stock, replacing processes that previously relied on batch updates. Transactions are reflected immediately across connected inventory and accounting systems, providing a more accurate and up-to-date view of stock throughout the trading day.
Using handheld devices, store partners can access current inventory information to support day-to-day activities including replenishment, stock management and markdown decisions.
Tesco
Tesco reports the roll-out of its 2,000th electric home delivery van, arriving last week at the retailer’s Hemsworth Superstore in West Yorkshire, where the store runs six of these vans.
Tesco has doubled the number of electric home delivery vans over the last year, with more than 30% of the fleet now powered by electricity. It is looking to transition to a fully electric fleet in the UK by the end of 2030.
Since introducing its first electric home delivery van in Greater London in 2020, its fleet of electric vehicles, powered by renewable electricity, has replaced millions of diesel delivery miles. It announced in October 2025 the deployment of its 1,000th electric home delivery van, which entered service at the Cardiff Extra store.
“The arrival of our 2,000th van at Hemsworth is another important milestone in our journey towards a fully electric home delivery fleet across the UK by 2030. Every new electric van we introduce helps us reduce emissions, improve local air quality and move closer to our goal of achieving net zero in our own operations by 2035. We're proud to be leading the way in the transition to low emissions home delivery for our customers,” says Nick Potter, Transport Distribution Director at Tesco.
El Caficultor
AuraVeo by Koenig & Bauer, in partnership with Appetite Creative, is launching a new connected packaging initiative with coffee brand, El Caficultor, turning coffee packs from a one off retail purchase to a direct sales and subscription channel. The new technology was showcased exclusively at London Packaging Week on 16th–17th September.
Each El Caficultor SKU has a unique code, which, when scanned, unlocks a mobile experience telling the coffee’s origin story, including its farm, altitude, processing method and sensory profile, before presenting the consumer with a discounted subscription offer. The initial roll-out spans El Caficultor’s 100% Arábica line: Cerrado Dulce (Brazil), Sidamo (Ethiopia), La Vereda (Colombia), and hero SKU Selva Negra (Nicaragua).
Through AuraVeo's cloud platform, consumers are guided through an immersive experience detailing cupping scores, varietals, and flavour characteristics, followed by a direct 10% discount on recurring subscription. With consumer consent, every interaction captures first-party data, giving the brand insights into purchasing behaviour across physical retail channels. Unlike static QR codes, AuraVeo's technology allows brands to update the code content without reprinting the packaging. Scans can also be tracked and attributed to the relevant product, giving El Caficultor visibility into how consumers interact with individual products and content.
Rather than placing codes on the back of the pack, Appetite Creative integrated the AuraVeo QR code directly within the front of pack country map illustrations paired with a clear call to action “ESCANEA Y AHORRA” (“Scan and Save”).
David's Bridal
David’s Bridal, a North American bridal and occasion retailer and Pearl, its AI powered platform, have announced the launch of Pearl Connect, pitched as the first AI vendor platform native to a couple’s wedding planning journey, putting everything a professional in this space needs to market, communicate and book into one touchpoint.
“Wedding professionals shouldn’t have to spend their days chasing emails, piecing together details and wondering which leads are actually worth their time,” says Kelly Cook, CEO at David’s Bridal. “We know what couples are planning, what they’re looking for, and where they are in their journey.”
“Pearl Connect puts that context to work for the businesses on the other side of the aisle. We’re simplifying all those disjointed ways of connecting into one place with the goal of removing any friction so wedding professionals can have a more meaningful, real connection with potential couples. It’s a very different way to think about a wedding vendor marketplace - it’s about vendor listings, it’s about creating real connections that can lead to revenue and growth for wedding pros.”
James Hall & Co.
Quadient has announced a partnership with James Hall & Co., SPAR UK’s primary retailer, wholesaler, and distributor for the North of England.
Parcel Pending by Quadient lockers are being rolled out across James Hall & Co.’s G&E Murgatroyd company owned retail estate, with 37 locations already live and further deployments planned across its network of stores. These offer 24/7 access for deliveries, returns, exchanges, and item storage. They support a range of services, including prescription collection, Click and Collect, key exchange, and spare parts retrieval.
“Through the company’s SPAR stores, partnering with James Hall & Co. Ltd allows us to further embed our open locker network into the fabric of local communities across the North of England,” says Katia Bourgeais-Crémel, EVP Parcel Locker Solutions Europe at Quadient. “Convenience retail plays a critical role in everyday life, and by introducing smart, secure lockers into these locations, we are removing friction from parcel collection and returns. This partnership reflects our focus on delivering predictable, scalable last-mile solutions that benefit the entire ecosystem from carriers and retailers to consumers and store staff.”
Fiona Drummond, Company Stores Director at James Hall & Co., says: “We are committed to enhancing the role our SPAR stores play within local communities, offering services that go beyond traditional retail. Partnering with Quadient enables us to introduce a secure and convenient parcel solution that meets the evolving needs of our customers, while driving additional footfall and value for our stores. We look forward to continuing the roll-out across our estate.”
Costco Wholesale
Costco Wholesale is expanding its payments partnership with Affirm to the UK. Eligible members shopping online can now choose Affirm’s BNPL offering at checkout and split the cost of their purchases into interest free or interest bearing monthly payments.
This builds on a partnership between the pair in the US, which launched in 2025.
"Getting the best value shouldn’t stop at the price tag. It should extend to how you pay, too,” says Ruth Spratt, UK Country Manager at Affirm. Our partnership with Costco gives UK members a simpler way to spread the cost of those big shops, with greater flexibility, no late fees, and no compounding interest.”
Nobody's Child
Nobody's Child has deployed Persi technology in its e-commerce offering. In a LinkedIn post, Liv Parkes, Founder and CEO at Persi, said: “This is a retailer that was on my wish list before Persi was much more than an idea. So seeing our technology live on their website feels pretty surreal.”
She added: “When you're building something new, you're asking people to take a chance on more than just a product. You're asking them to believe in where it could go. And from our earliest conversations, Nobody’s Child did exactly that. They saw the opportunity for styling to become a much bigger part of the e-commerce experience, and trusted our small team to build it with them.”
Customers can now use Persi in two ways: PDP Style Bundle - multiple, completely shoppable ways to wear an item, whilst discovering complementary pieces complete the look; AI Stylist - personalised outfits based on their style, occasion and what they're looking for, including the ability to style something they already own.
Parkes commented: “Both helping answer one of the simplest (and most important) questions in fashion e-commerce: "I like it. But how would I wear it?" Seeing Persi live on a retailer of this scale is a VERY proud founder moment. But I'm even more grateful for the people who were willing to say yes.”
Yoti
Yoti has announced partnerships with technology providers including Diebold Nixdorf, Flooid, StrongPoint, Kestronics, and Zebra Technologies to help UK supermarkets, retailers and hospitality businesses introduce digital age checks for alcohol sales.
This follows a change in the law allowing Yoti ID and Post Office EasyID, as well as other digital IDs certified to the UK government’s Digital Verification Services (DVS) Trust Framework, to be used as proof of age when buying alcohol in licensed premises.
Diebold Nixdorf, Flooid, StrongPoint, Kestronics and Zebra Technologies provide point of sale and self-checkout technology to UK supermarkets, retail and hospitality businesses. Through the tie up, they will integrate digital ID checks into their existing systems.
For smaller independent retailers and licensed premises, Yoti has a free ID Checker mobile and web app and a partnership with Licensing Connect. The app allows staff to check that a customer’s digital proof of age is authentic and valid. More than 15,000 businesses downloaded the ID Checker app ahead of the change in law.
ALICE + OLIVIA
ALICE + OLIVIA has launched an AI powered “See Yourself in the Show” experience at the brand’s Spring 2027 New York Fashion Week presentation. This allowed attendees to see themselves in the new collection as it debuted.
The activation tapped Glance’s AI powered virtual try-on technology.
“Fashion has always been about imagination and possibility, and AI is opening up an entirely new way to bring that creativity to life,” says Stacey Bendet, Founder, CEO and Creative Director of ALICE + OLIVIA. “Partnering with Glance allowed us to blend technology and fashion in a way that feels innovative, immersive, and exciting for the future.”
“ALICE + OLIVIA is a visionary brand and one of the first names in fashion to treat a collection debut as something the audience participates in rather than watches passively,” says Naveen Tewari, Founder and CEO at InMobi and Glance. “That sense of immediacy and excitement is at the heart of Glance's AI enabled agentic commerce experience and is key to how consumers want to discover and shop for fashion today.”
M&S
Over 350 M&S Food stores now offer Too Good To Go Surprise Bags made up of surplus bakery products, giving customers the chance to collect food at a reduced price at the end of the day directly from in-store bakeries.
Too Good To Go is an app for surplus food. The national launch follows a trial in a select number of locations across the UK and is the latest move in M&S Food’s work to reduce food waste and ensure good food doesn’t go to waste. The Surprise Bags will include the likes of pastries, cookies and bread baked in-store. Each will include three to four products to a minimum retail price of £10.20 for £3.80. Customers can order them through the aforementioned app and collect them Monday to Saturday, one hour before their local store closes.
The partnership sits alongside M&S’s wider Plan A programme to halve food waste by 2030 and to help edible surplus food find its way to a dinner plate.
Lucinda Langton, Head of Sustainability at M&S Food, says: “Too Good To Go is a brilliant example of how we’re turning our commitment to reducing food waste into practical action. By giving customers access to surprise bags of surplus bakery products, we can help ensure more of our food is enjoyed. The response from our trial stores has been outstanding, and this partnership is another positive step towards our goal of halving food waste by 2030.”
PSC
Philippine Seven Corporation (PSC), the exclusive operator of 7-Eleven convenience stores in the Philippines, is utilising forecasting and replenishment from RELEX Solutions across its 27 distribution centres (DCs). The implementation is being delivered in partnership with genieX.
7-Eleven is the world’s largest convenience store chain, with over 83,000 outlets in 17 countries. In the Philippines, PSC oversees all 7-Eleven operations nationwide. By implementing RELEX’s forecasting and replenishment capabilities, it will replace its spreadsheet-based processes with automated, data driven planning to improve supplier collaboration, increase fill rates, and upgrade operational efficiency.
“For over four decades, PSC has worked to make 7-Eleven a trusted part of everyday life for Filipinos,” says Victor Paterno, Chair at Philippine Seven Corporation. “As we continue to expand and digitalise, partnering with RELEX and genieX enables us to strengthen our supply chain foundation and plan more effectively for the future.”
The Estée Lauder Companies
The Estée Lauder Companies has announced a partnership with Profound, providing it with visibility into how its brands are represented across leading generative AI platforms, as well as opportunities to optimise that representation. It becomes the first in prestige beauty to deploy Profound’s capabilities globally across the company’s full portfolio and operationalise generative engine optimisation (GEO) and AI marketing at scale.
“The way people discover beauty is being rewritten in real-time, and we intend to shape that shift rather than reacting to it,” says Aude Gandon, Global Chief Digital & Marketing Officer, The Estée Lauder Companies.
“This partnership gives every brand in our portfolio the ability to show up distinctly, consistently, and accurately wherever our consumers are asking for recommendations. Our work with Profound is a natural extension of how we already think about culture, community, and commerce working together, and it puts us at the front of an industry wide transition.”
Amazon
Amazon has launched Just Walk Out technology powered stores across venues Soldier Field, Kroger Field/Kentucky Wildcats and Spartan Stadium/Michigan State Athletics.
In a LinkedIn post, Wes Moon, Sr. Tech Business Development Manager, Just Walk Out Technology - Sports & Entertainment, Amazon, said: "We've now surpassed 400 stores globally, hundreds of these deployed across sports and entertainment venues - milestones for this game-changing tech that wouldn't be possible without game-changing partners like Levy Restaurants & Gallery."
He added: "Our focus remains on optimising the fan experience: getting fans back to their seats faster, reducing wait times, and making every visit seamless from entry to exit. Reach out if you are interested in learning how Just Walk Out technology can transform experiences at your venue."
Tesco and Uber Eats
Running through to 20th September, Tesco and Uber Eats are launching Doorbell Drops, an exclusive selection of hosting essentials available at half-price to Clubcard members.
Customers can visit the Doorbell Drops hub page for Tesco on the Uber Eats app to shop the likes of Tesco Finest All Butter Sultana Scones, alongside strawberry jam and clotted cream, Mcvities Chocolate Digestives, Président French Brie with Jacobs crackers and Tesco Green Olives with Slow Roasted Tomatoes.
Merve Basci, Uber Eats UK General Manager, says: "Unannounced visits used to be a staple of British social and community life, but the fear of being unprepared and judged for stale biscuits is driving many to hide rather than host. Whether it’s dodging in-laws or frantically scouring the fridge for something edible to serve, our new partnership with Tesco can help people ditch the ‘doorbell dread’, so that young people especially can relax and enter their hosting era with more confidence."
Suzanne Quinn, Tesco Customer Director, says: “We’re always looking for little helps that make life easier for customers, and expanding our rapid delivery service through our Uber Eats partnership is another way we’re helping the nation get what they need, when they need it. The Doorbell Deals range has been created for those moments when plans change or guests arrive at short notice, giving customers quick access to fresh food, drink, and hosting essentials, so they can conveniently pull together a delicious spread in minutes.”
The launch follows Tesco’s recent partnership with Uber Eats, with the aim of extending rapid grocery delivery, Clubcard Prices and Clubcard points to more customers across the UK.

items.body:
Grocery and sports retail represent the largest sectors of untapped loyalty value, HyperFinity finds
51 of the UK’s leading retailers are collectively missing out on £806.9 million in gross margin each year through loyalty programmes that fail to convert member engagement into genuine commercial return, according to HyperFinity research.
This finds that the average retailer is sitting on £15.8 million of untapped gross margin opportunity tied up in underperforming loyalty programmes. Crucially, the analysis shows this is not a crisis of customer loyalty itself, but a crisis of execution.
Recent consumer research from HyperFinity found that 91% of shoppers use their loyalty programmes on every visit or most visits, and 79% want more personalised offers. However, the intelligence to turn that participation into genuine commercial value remains largely untapped.
HyperFinity says it has identified three failure modes that appear most consistently across underperforming programmes: Redemption friction: where personalised rewards cannot actually be used by the customer; Value erosion: programmes dilute their value over time and customers no longer feel recognised or personally rewarded; App performance: where technical issues can undermine the loyalty experience at key moments of engagement. Between them, these three issues account for the vast majority of loyalty underperformance across the 51 retailers analysed.
Grocery and sports retail represent the largest sectors of untapped loyalty value in the analysis. In grocery, where loyalty programmes are near-universal and consumer expectations are high, the gap between programme promise and programme delivery is particularly pronounced. In sports retail, high basket values and strong brand affinity mean the commercial cost of underperformance is further amplified.
Across all retail sectors, a consistent and telling pattern emerges. Programmes that score well with consumers on sentiment are still leaking serious commercial value, often because the mechanics of earning and redeeming rewards break down at the point of transaction. The analysis also surfaces a subtler challenge. Some programmes that perform well on consumer sentiment are still failing to translate that engagement into incremental behaviour.
Consumers, meanwhile, have already signalled their readiness for personalised loyalty. Separate HyperFinity research found that 69% of shoppers are comfortable with retailers using AI to personalise loyalty offers. For retailers, the opportunity is to use that technology to deliver genuinely relevant value - rewarding customers on the products they already love, while introducing them to new products and categories they’re likely to value. Those that get this right can turn loyalty into a true competitive advantage, HyperFinity argues.
Thomas Hill, Co-founder at HyperFinity, comments: “The loyalty opportunity in UK retail has never been greater. Customers value loyalty programmes, which is a powerful driver of loyalty in return. But to realise that opportunity, retailers need to recognise customers as individuals and give them offers that make them feel valued and rewarded.”
“Our research found that 44% of shoppers say they will stay loyal to a retailer even during periods of economic pressure, if the rewards are genuinely worthwhile. At a time when consumers are more price conscious than ever, loyalty should be about more than simply offering discounts. It should be about using customer insight to understand what people genuinely value and delivering experiences and products that feel relevant to them.”
So hot right now
HyperFinity is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…

items.body:
Ravelin flags the rise of the refundjacker as dishonesty becomes normalised among shoppers
Refundjacking - where shoppers gain from a company’s refund policies - is becoming one of e-commerce’s biggest challenges. New research from fraud prevention platform Ravelin revealed 27% of people openly admit to abusing refund policies.
The research is based on a survey of 6,282 consumers, drawn from the UK (2,115), Germany (2,095), and France (2,072) who have shopped online in the last six months.
98% of attempts to take advantage of these systems are successful. 37% of UK consumers have engaged in, or plan to engage in, refund abuse, according to the major European markets surveyed, making the UK the highest rate of refundjacking - higher than France (33%) and Germany (25%).
Behaviours include gaming refund and return polices, falsely claiming goods never arrived, returning items after using them or sending back empty boxes or dummy returns while keeping the original product. Research shows that occasional abusers are earning an average of €/£390 per claim, where shoppers who abuse the policies more than four times a year can an average of €/£491 per claim.
The British Retail Consortium’s Policy Advisor for Finance, Chris Owen, comments “The growth of refund abuse is putting unnecessary financial drain on retailers at a time when margins are already under intense pressure. The result is lost revenue and higher costs, meaning everyone ends up paying more. It’s a serious problem which requires serious attention. The BRC is working with our members and others to tackle this growing problem.”
“This is no longer a fringe behaviour,” says Martin Sweeney, CEO at Ravelin. “Our research shows refund abuse becoming more prevalent and normalised. People aren’t sneaking around the edges of policy anymore - they’re openly breaking the rules, sharing tips on how to cheat the system, and justifying it as fair game. Merchants face a challenge to balance great experiences for good customers, while discouraging or blocking abusive behaviours.”
AI is enabling refund abusers and making them harder to detect by automating letters to customer service or generating fake images to falsify evidence. Despite the scale of the issue, many e-commerce brands continue to rely on blanket responses. By tightening policies across the board, merchants risk making shopping harder for all customers and undermining brand loyalty, Ravelin argues.
75% of shoppers polled in its study agree that those who abuse refund policies make online shopping less pleasant or less convenient for honest customers. Making the right judgment call on refund abuse can be difficult. The research suggests many refund abusers would desist if merchants were tougher with them.
Sweeney says: “The most efficient response involves using your own data to your advantage. The better a merchant understands the different cohorts of refund abusers, the more they can tailor their approaches to the problem. Blanket rules treat every customer as a risk - and that simply doesn’t work anymore. Retailers need to focus on behaviour, intent and patterns over time. When you target abuse more intelligently, you protect revenue without undermining the shopping experience for everyone else – and that’s the balance the industry now has to strike.”

items.title: Business rates cut will ‘backfire’ for Soho and West End
items.summary: John Healey’s plans to deliver an emergency tax cut for high street businesses would fail to boost most firms in London’s busiest areas like Soho and the West End, analysis suggests. The Chancellor is reportedly planning to cut taxes for pubs, shops, cafes and restaurants by hiking the threshold for small business rates relief (SBBR).   [...]
items.body:
Business rates cut will ‘backfire’ for Soho and West End
John Healey’s plans to deliver an emergency tax cut for high street businesses would fail to boost most firms in London’s busiest areas like Soho and the West End, analysis suggests.
The Chancellor is reportedly planning to cut taxes for pubs, shops, cafes and restaurants by hiking the threshold for small business rates relief (SBBR).
The SBBR currently exempts all businesses with a ratable value – which is based on their property – of less than £12,000. Healey is considering hiking the threshold in line with inflation to £17,096.
But analysis shared exclusively with City AM has shown that this tax break would mainly benefit retail and hospitality firms on the outskirts of London, having almost no effect on the areas of the capital which currently face the highest rents and tax burden.
Out of London’s 110,000 retail, hospitality and leisure businesses, 17.5 per cent have a rateable value between £12,000 and £17,096 and would therefore benefit from the new relief, according to data from knowyourrates.co.uk.
Tax cut ‘for Sutton, not Soho’
While this proportion rises to 26.5 per cent in Sutton and 26.2 per cent in Barking, only 3.8 per cent of premises in Westminster, which includes famous shopping and hospitality districts like Soho and the West End, would benefit from this relief.
Only seven of Soho’s 1,102 shops, cafes, pubs and restaurants would have their business rates scrapped under the change. In the West End, 43 of the area’s 8,974 premises would benefit from the tax cut.
Just six businesses on Oxford Street – out of 256 retail, hospitality and leisure firms in Europe’s busiest shopping destination – would see their bills cut by the change.
The tax cut would apply to only 3.9 per cent of premises in the City of London, 4.3 per cent in Kensington & Chelsea and 9.3 per cent in Camden.
Alan Fang, the creator of knowyourrates.co.uk, said this data shows that the tax cut is an “outer-London measure”. He added: “Raise the threshold and you help the parade in Sutton and do almost nothing for Soho. That may be the right call, but nobody should think it is a West End rescue.”
A number of top retail and hospitality bodies told City AM this data proves that Healey must go further to tackle the tax burden facing high streets. Dee Corsi, chief executive of the New West End Company, said that the cut to thresholds would “backfire” for the district’s retail and hospitality firms.
“We need a policy framework that recognises the significant value of these businesses to our national economy, as when flagship stores perform, high streets across the country benefit,” she said. The West End generates £17bn in tax each year and pays eight per cent of the UK’s business rates, she added.
Healey must ‘fix the flaws of business rates’
Ros Morgan, chief executive of the Heart of London Business Alliance, told City AM: “Raising the small business rates threshold may provide welcome support for some premises, but it will do little for the vast majority of businesses in central London and other town and city centres, where property costs and rates bills are particularly high.
“The West End is a major economic engine for London and the UK, supporting hundreds of thousands of jobs and generating billions in economic activity. We cannot afford to leave businesses in these vital centres behind.”
The data also reveals that the hike to business rates thresholds would fail to deliver tax cuts to most of London’s pubs.
Around 84 per cent of pubs in the capital sit above the £17,096 threshold, with an average rateable value of £58,500. Nine per cent of hospitality businesses in London would be caught by the tax relief, compared to 20 per cent of shops.
Allen Simpson, chief executive of UK Hospitality, said: “These figures show why business rates reform needs to work for businesses of all sizes. Pubs, restaurants and hotels of all shapes, sizes and rateable values employ significant numbers of people, with hotels particularly exposed to rising rates costs.”
HM Treasury was contacted for comment.

items.title: Fast fashion copyright battle continues as Shein granted appeal against Temu
items.summary: Fast fashion retailer Shein has been granted permission to appeal against rival Temu in a first-of-its-kind copyright battle in the UK. A judge confirmed in a hearing on Monday that Shein can challenge a judgement handed down last month in the Court of Appeal. The judge said there were “compelling reasons” for the court to [...]
items.body:
Fast fashion copyright battle continues as Shein granted appeal against Temu
Fast fashion retailer Shein has been granted permission to appeal against rival Temu in a first-of-its-kind copyright battle in the UK.
A judge confirmed in a hearing on Monday that Shein can challenge a judgement handed down last month in the Court of Appeal.
The judge said there were “compelling reasons” for the court to consider the appeal as it marks the first time a UK court has had to consider how rules regarding copyright apply to online marketplaces.
The fast fashion retailer originally brought the claim to the High Court in 2023 after sending a letter to Temu in June asking for 2,559 photographs to be removed, as the retailer claimed these were taken by its own employees, as well as freelancers, agencies or suppliers. Shein alleged Temu had used them without permission.
The online retailer argued the photographs were examples of “infringements of its copyright on a substantial scale”, and that Temu had presented the images as if they were the company’s own and did not make clear that images were posted by sellers, so it cannot swerve responsibility for copyright.
However, the judge, Mrs Justice Bacon, said in her judgment last month that Shein UK did not own the copyright of the employee photographs at the time it sent the letter to Temu, as the companies were employed by Shein UK’s Chinese counterpart, Guangzhou Shein.
The judge ruled that Temu suffered a loss when it had to remove “thousands” of product listings from its website following the letter and court proceedings.
On Monday, Shein UK argued the judge had not properly considered whether Temu was actually liable for how it publicly displays photographs on its website.
Michael Bloch, KC, representing Shein UK, said that unlike videos posted by users on YouTube which are clearly not owned by the site, Temu “made no mention of sellers and gave the impression that the products on sale were being supplied by Temu”.
Charlotte May KC, representing Whaleco UK, the company which runs Temu, said Shein UK’s points could have been raised at the original trial and the judge had not made any mistakes in her judgment.
“I consider Mr Bloch’s argument just about meets the threshold for real prospect of success for the purposes of permission to appeal,” Mrs Justice Bacon said.
“Given this is the first UK case to consider the application of a hosting defence to an online marketplace it seems to me a compelling reason for the Court of Appeal to consider this matter,” she said.
The judge also ordered that Shein UK publish a message on their supplier portal informing customers about the court’s original judgement, which should be pinned to the top of the page or reposted every week for six months.
Shein’s third IPO attempt
This follows Shein at the start of September listing in Hong Kong in a price-cut initial public offering (IPO) after two failed attempts in both London and New York.
Shein and Temu were contacted for comment.

●  Prada Paradigme Le Parfum
Prada turns up the intensity with Paradigme Le Parfum, bringing a deeper interpretation to the Paradigme collection. Rich and sophisticated with an addictive warmth, it offers a distinctive option for anyone looking to discover something new this festive season.
●  Carolina Herrera La Bomba Eau de Parfum
Playful, vibrant and designed to be noticed, La Bomba brings together an uplifting mix of fruity, floral and warm notes. With its statement-making bottle and joyful character, it’s a standout choice for gifting this Christmas.
●  Chanel Coco Mademoiselle Eau de Parfum
Some perfumes never go out of style. Coco Mademoiselle remains a firm favourite, with its instantly recognisable combination of fresh citrus, elegant florals and warm, sensual notes making it a timeless addition to Christmas wish lists.
●  Prada Paradoxe Eau de Parfum
A modern favourite that continues to win over perfume lovers, Prada Paradoxe balances bright white florals with warm amber and musk. Elegant yet distinctive and refillable for sustainable conscious shoppers, it has firmly established itself as a go-to choice for gifting.
●  Gucci Flora Gorgeous Orchid Intense EDP
A richer addition to Gucci’s Flora collection, Gorgeous Orchid Intense offers a more indulgent take on the floral scent family. Warm, creamy and enveloping, it’s a perfume predicted to catch the attention of shoppers looking for something a little different this Christmas.
●  Yves Saint Laurent LIBRE Eau de Parfum
A modern icon that continues to hold its place among perfume lovers, YSL LIBRE combines aromatic lavender with orange blossom and warm vanilla. Its distinctive floral character has made it an enduring favourite and a go-to gift year after year.
Andrea Rickard, trading director at The Perfume Shop, said: “Christmas is one of the most exciting times of the year for perfume, and we always love seeing which scents our customers are adding to their wish lists. “What’s particularly exciting this year is the amount of choice available. We’re seeing established favourites continue to resonate with customers, while newer scents are also capturing their attention. Whether you’re shopping for someone who knows exactly what they love or hoping to surprise them with something new, there really is something for everyone this Christmas.”
“The Perfume Shop will also offer a range of perfume gift sets, stocking fillers and festive offers throughout Spritzmas, alongside personalisation services including bottle engraving and personalised ribbons, helping shoppers add an extra special touch to their Christmas gifting.”

items.title: Waitrose extends Tony’s Open Chain partnership
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Waitrose has announced a major expansion of its partnership with Tony’s Open Chain, scaling up its action to source cocoa responsibly across its seasonal and boxed chocolate lines. Under the expanded agreement, over half of Waitrose seasonal chocolate will now be sourced via Tony’s Open Chain Mass Balance. This transition also involves strengthening the sourcing […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Waitrose has announced a major expansion of its partnership with Tony’s Open Chain, scaling up its action to source cocoa responsibly across its seasonal and boxed chocolate lines.
Under the expanded agreement, over half of Waitrose seasonal chocolate will now be sourced via Tony’s Open Chain Mass Balance. This transition also involves strengthening the sourcing credentials of its own-label boxed chocolates using the Tony’s Open Chain mass balance “Bean to Machine” sourcing model for the first time in addition to its existing Fairtrade Certified Cocoa sourcing.
The expansion builds on Waitrose’s landmark 2024 agreement, when it became the first UK based retailer to join Tony’s Open Chain as a ‘Mission Ally’. The initial rollout covered six Waitrose own-brand chocolate bars and three Cook’s ingredients bars using segregated cocoa.
Marija Rompani, director of ethics & sustainability at John Lewis Partnership comments: “We’re proud to extend our partnership with Tony’s Chocolonely through Tony’s Open Chain. Enhancing our responsible sourcing standards is an essential part of building resilient supply chains that deliver the high-quality ethically sourced products our customers expect, both now and in the future.
“By broadening our sourcing of cocoa through Tony’s Open Chain, we hope to show what’s possible and to encourage other retailers and brands to join in its shared mission to help end exploitation in the cocoa supply chain once and for all.”
Rianne van Doeveren, General Manager at Tony’s Open Chain comments:
“When we talk about impact, we’re talking about real families in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire whose livelihoods depend on cocoa. Waitrose’s extension of their partnership with Tony’s Open Chain is not symbolic, it’s a practical change. More cocoa will be flowing through a supply chain that commits to higher cocoa prices for the long term, traces the beans sourced, and invests directly in the communities that grow them.
These farmers deserve partners who show up properly, and that’s exactly what Waitrose is doing. We thank Waitrose for their trust, dedication and passion in expanding the volume of cocoa sourced via our impact model, and proving that it’s possible to create more equitable supply chains.”
By deepening its involvement, Waitrose reinforces its support for Tony’s Open Chain’s Sourcing Principles:
- 100% Traceable Beans: Ensuring complete visibility over where cocoa is grown and its journey through the supply chain up to at least the first cocoa processor, prior to mass-balance mixing.
- A Higher Price: Committing to pay the Living Income Reference Price for cocoa to help bridge the gap to a living income for farmers.
- Strong Co-operatives: Investing in professionalisation of farmer cooperatives to empower local communities.
- Long-Term Commitments: Working with suppliers on multi-year agreements to offer income security.
- Quality & Productivity: Supporting farmers to improve yield and agricultural practices safely.
All Tony’s Open Chain cocoa remains Fairtrade certified as well. As part of Waitrose’s ambition to close the living income gap, the retailer pays an additional premium on top of the Fairtrade certified bean price to achieve the Living Income Reference Price, a benchmark set by Fairtrade International.
While the sourcing models advance, the products themselves remain unchanged in taste and quality. Customers will continue to enjoy the exact same recipes and flavours across Waitrose chocolate bars, Cook’s ingredients, seasonal treats, and boxed chocolates, with the added assurance of ethically sourced cocoa.
* Since the 2023-2024 cocoa season

The Toy Retailers Association is recruiting eight children from across the UK to become official Mini Toy Testers, giving […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Calling all future toy critics! The hunt is on for a team of Mini Toy Testers to put the UK’s most sought-after Christmas toys through their paces before they appear on wish lists across the country.
The Toy Retailers Association is recruiting eight children from across the UK to become official Mini Toy Testers, giving them exclusive early access to toys tipped to be among this year’s biggest festive hits as part of the coveted DreamToys list.
Successful applicants will unbox, play with and review toys from the industry’s leading brands, sharing their honest verdicts to help identify the stand-out stars of Christmas 2026. Better still, each Mini Toy Tester will be paid in toys – receiving all fifteen of the toys they test as a reward for their hard-earned judging, and just in time for Christmas.
The DreamToys list is the UK’s most authoritative prediction of the most desirable new toys on the high street and is selected by a panel of independent toy retailers and experts from small independents to national chains.
Applications are open for children aged 3-12 and parents or guardians can apply on their child’s behalf via the online form at www.toyretailersassociation.co.uk/mini-toy-testers before midnight on Saturday 17 October.
Paul Reader, Chairman of the DreamToys Selection Panel at the Toy Retailers Association, said: “Each year, the DreamToys list shines a spotlight on the toys that are set to capture children’s imaginations and become the must-have gifts at Christmas.
“After the incredible response to last year’s search for our Mini Toy Testers, we couldn’t wait to bring it back. Children are the ultimate toy experts, they’re honest, imaginative and know exactly what makes a toy fun, exciting and worthy of a place on their Christmas wish list.
“We look forward to welcoming this year’s panel of Mini Toy Testers to put the toys through their paces and help us spread the word about the most exciting new products to hit the shelves this Christmas.”
For more information, or to apply on behalf of a child, parents or guardians can visit www.toyretailersassociation.co.uk/mini-toy-testers. T&Cs apply.

Baileys Chocolate is set to support retailers capitalise on Christmas demand with the launch of its 2026 festive collection, introducing an exciting new product alongside the return of its best-selling favourites. With Baileys enjoying over 94% brand awareness in the UK and recognised as the UK’s most loved spirits brand[1], the range is designed to […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Baileys Chocolate is set to support retailers capitalise on Christmas demand with the launch of its 2026 festive collection, introducing an exciting new product alongside the return of its best-selling favourites. With Baileys enjoying over 94% brand awareness in the UK and recognised as the UK’s most loved spirits brand[1], the range is designed to capitalise on demand for premium yet accessible gifting and self-treat occasions.
Leading the line-up is the brand-new Baileys Chocolate Advent Calendar (90g), expanding the Baileys range into the popular seasonal advent calendar format. It offers 24 days of smooth milk chocolate buttons infused with the unmistakable flavour of Baileys Original Irish Cream. Tapping into the key seasonal countdown period, the accessible price point makes it an ideal adult indulgence during the build up to Christmas Day. Available at Sainsbury’s and other selected retailers, RRP £3.50.
The popular Baileys Chocolate Caramel Whirls, first launched in 2025, will be available in both single and three-pack formats. Following strong consumer demand last year, the indulgent combination of milk chocolate, fluffy mallow and velvety caramel, all infused with the flavour of Baileys Original Irish Cream is expected to be another seasonal success. Following its successful launch, Baileys Chocolate Caramel Whirls were awarded Gold at The Grocer New Product & Packaging Awards 2025, recognising the product’s innovation & uniqueness. Available in retailers including Sainsbury’s, Tesco, Morrisons, Ocado, Waitrose, Lidl, Asda and more, RRP £1.00 (single) and £2.75 (three-pack).
Also available this Christmas are the much-loved Baileys Original Irish Cream Truffles (135g), featuring rich milk chocolate shells filled with the brand’s signature Baileys truffle filling. Following a packaging update in 2025, the deluxe gifting favourite is now presented in fully recyclable paper twist wraps, continuing to offer strong appeal for both sharing and seasonal gifting. The move will see Lir Chocolates remove 13,000kg of non-recyclable plastic from the market annually, the equivalent of 66 million fewer plastic wrappers entering the market each year. Available from Sainsbury’s, Asda, Ocado, Lidl and selected retailers, RRP £5.25.
The luxury Baileys Chocolate Collection Box (175g) will also be back, an assortment of milk, white and dark chocolates infused with the iconic taste of Baileys Original Irish Cream and featuring a selection of luxury fillings. With fully recyclable packaging, the Collection Box remains a standout gifting option. Available in selected retailers Including Waitrose and Sainsbury’s, RRP £7.00.
Completing the collection are the Baileys Christmas Tree Truffle Tin (228g) and Baileys Christmas Truffle Box (100g), both filled with Baileys’ signature Original Irish Cream Truffles. Featuring refreshed packaging for 2026 with a striking winter scene, they offer an eye-catching gifting option for the festive season, with an RRP starting at £5.00 and available at selected retailers including Card Factory and Iceland
Ethan Duffey, brand manager at Lir Chocolates, said: “Christmas remains the biggest opportunity for premium chocolate, and our 2026 Baileys Chocolate collection has been developed to help retailers maximise every gifting and self-treat occasion throughout the season. With the introduction of our first Baileys Chocolate Advent Calendar and the return of Baileys Whirls following a strong first year in 2025, the range combines exciting new formats with proven favourites. Supported by the strength of Baileys as a household brand, the collection brings together new launches and festive favourites to offer consumers even more ways to enjoy the iconic Baileys taste at Christmas.”
Baileys Chocolate delivers 52% growth at Christmas and continues to establish itself as one of the fastest-growing premium chocolate brands during the festive season. Supported by the trust and familiarity of the Baileys brand, the 2026 Christmas collection driving seasonal sales growth across gifting occasions.

The three SKU range comprises Local Living Cupcake Kit (PMP £2.29), Local Living Brownie Mix (PMP £1.99) and Local Living Batter Mix (PMP £0.69), offering retailers a ready-made baking range built around easy-to-use mixes.

That’s what Local Living is all about.”

items.title: Man jailed after robbing Middlesbrough convenience store at knife-point
items.summary: In June 2026, Jason Dixon, of Falkland Street in Middlesbrough, entered Go Local, on The Gardens in Beechwood, demanding money while producing and waving a knife towards an employee. The 50-year-old man then stole three bottles of alcohol and left the store in a hurry… This story continues at Man jailed after robbing Middlesbrough convenience store at knife-point Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The 50-year-old man then stole three bottles of alcohol and left the store in a hurry by fleeing on a bicycle – falling off once before fully cycling away.
After locking the door, the employee called police who swiftly attended. A knife was handed to an officer by a member of the public after being dropped by Dixon.
He was located and arrested on suspicion of robbery. After being questioned in custody he was subsequently charged.
Dixon appeared at Teesside Crown Court this month to be sentenced to three years and four months. He was also given an indefinite restraining order.
Following the sentencing, Detective Ramzan, from Middlesbrough CID, said: “I want to commend the bravery shown by the victim during this incident. Their composure helped ensure this was reported quickly — and that made all the difference.
“I also want to highlight how swiftly officers responded. Thanks to this, the offender was identified, arrested and brought before the courts without delay.
“I hope this serves as a clear reminder, that if you commit an offence, you will be dealt with robustly.”

items.title: Fed partners with payments provider Lopay
items.summary: The Federation of Independent Retailers (the Fed) has teamed up with payments provider Lopay to offer members preferential card processing rates that it said could save typical businesses almost £3,000 a year. Fed members have exclusive access to the free Lopay Zero Card. For every… This story continues at Fed partners with payments provider Lopay Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Fed members have exclusive access to the free Lopay Zero Card. For every £1 a member spends on stock through the Zero Card, at their usual wholesalers and cash & carries, Lopay will process £1 of customer card payments with zero processing fees.
Members don’t need to change how they buy stock to benefit. It’s the everyday spend they already make that unlocks the savings.
Combined with the Fed’s preferential Lopay rate, the offer also includes a free business account with instant access to card takings, a card terminal from £9.99 a month with fully transparent pricing, and no contracts or exit fees, so members can switch with confidence, and leave just as easily if it isn’t right for them. Onboarding and ongoing support are UK-based.
Lopay founder and chief executive Richard Carter said: “For businesses, combining the Fed’s preferential Lopay rate with the Zero Card could mean reducing the amount they spend on payment processing by 60 to 70 per cent or more. And those savings add up quickly.
“For a typical business paying around £300 a month in card processing fees, Lopay and the Zero Card could bring that figure down to around £55 a month – putting almost £3,000 a year back into the business.”
The Fed’s national president Hemanshu Patel said: ““At a time when the cost of trading is rising, we are pleased to have teamed up with Lopay to give Fed members access to preferential rates and an additional way to potentially reduce their card processing costs
“As with any business service, we would encourage members to look at the offer carefully, consider their own circumstances and make sure it is right for their business.”

items.title: Fears over interest rate rise and jobs send UK consumer confidence to three-year low
items.summary: Blow to John Healey before budget as UK households face ‘notable strain’ on their finances Business live – latest updates Fears of a steep rise in mortgage payments and increasing job insecurity have sent UK consumer confidence tumbling to a three-month low, according to a leading survey. In a blow to John Healey before next month’s budget, the S&P Global consumer sentiment index dropped to 42.7 in September from 42.9 in August, indicating “a notable strain on financial confidence across UK households”. Continue reading...
items.body:
Fears of a steep rise in mortgage payments and increasing job insecurity have sent UK consumer confidence tumbling to a three-month low, according to a leading survey.
In a blow to John Healey before next month’s budget, the S&P Global consumer sentiment index dropped to 42.7 in September from 42.9 in August, indicating “a notable strain on financial confidence across UK households”.
The chancellor could announce tax rises in his first budget to offset the rising cost of government borrowing, which has soared in response to the conflict in the Middle East.
S&P Global said consumers were concerned about the likelihood of an increase in interest rates by the Bank of England. More than 50% of 1,500 respondents said they expected a rise in the cost of borrowing over the next year.
Fixed-rate mortgage costs have already jumped to multi-year highs in the UK, while the threat of artificial intelligence and caution among employers about hiring new staff sent consumer confidence in the jobs market plunging to its lowest level in three-and-a-half years.
The average two-year fixed residential mortgage rate rose to 5.88% on Monday, its highest since 16 April and up from 5.84% last Friday, while the average five-year is at its highest since October 2023, at 5.92%, up from 5.88%, data from Moneyfacts showed.
The rise in mortgage costs is expected to add about £150 to monthly mortgage payments, based on a typical loan of £250,000 over 25 years, since the start of March 2026.
Official figures have shown that the average direct debit to cover monthly mortgage costs has risen over the past four years from about £600 to £900.
Maryam Baluch, an economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said a downbeat mood was spreading across UK households “as improved sentiment surrounding the new government is eroded by renewed worries over energy prices, the cost of living and job prospects”.
She said: “Against a backdrop of rising volatility in energy markets linked to tensions in the Middle East, households increasingly reported difficulties accessing credit, suggesting that expectations of tighter monetary conditions are beginning to feed through to borrowing conditions. Together, these factors point to cautiousness about both financial prospects and pose some downside risks to the broader economic outlook.”
Analysts believe the jobs market has proved resilient since the US attack on Iran and a steep rise in the cost of fuel and energy, but a steady decline in the number of payrolled employees over the past six months and a drop in vacancies to a five-year low have shown employers are worried about their profitability over the next year.
The British Chamber of Commerce has called for the government to give businesses extra support after a series of tax rises over the past two years, including an increase in employers national insurance payments.
A survey by the business organisation of 5,000 companies in the second quarter of 2026 found that only 17% were planning to increase investment in the coming months, a post-pandemic low.
Last week, Andy Burnham said he will need to take “difficult decisions” on the economy to ensure that it “remains on track”.
In response to the growing clamour for tax cuts to support businesses and households hit by the cost of living crisis, the Liberal Democrat leader, Ed Davey, said at his party conference that the UK should cut fuel duty to offset some of the rise in petrol and diesel prices at the pumps.
The German government on Monday announced plans for a cut in tax on fuel of about 15p to take effect on 1 October.
Healey could limit his tax rises to wealthier groups, including a rise in capital gains tax. However, analysts say he is unlikely to raise sufficient funds from discreet tax rises to pay for higher defence spending and the rise in debt costs while preserving a reserve buffer, often referred to as headroom, of at least £20bn.

items.summary: PepsiCo is helping retailers get their savoury snacking aisles festive-ready with a seasonal line up of reskins, alongside four bold limited-edition launches. With Christmas packs landing on shelves from 28 September across Walkers, Doritos, Sensations and Wotsits Giants, PepsiCo’s seasonal activity brings together familiar favourites… This story continues at PepsiCo unveils Christmas 2026 savoury snacking line-up Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
With Christmas packs landing on shelves from 28 September across Walkers, Doritos, Sensations and Wotsits Giants, PepsiCo’s seasonal activity brings together familiar favourites and festive flavours.
Fan favourites remain key for Walkers, Doritos and Sensations during Christmas, with core flavours having accounted for more than 95% of total crisp sales in 2025, according to Nielsen IQ data.
Designed with clear Christmas cues, such as Christmas trees, stars and festive baubles, the reskins bring a festive twist to some of PepsiCo’s biggest core snacks.
Pepsico said this will help popular SKUs stand out on shelf, giving retailers a strong seasonal offering to compliment the new flavour launches.
The limited-edition range includes Doritos Gingerbread, back for a second year after generating more than one million organic TikTok views last Christmas.
Sensations Honey Glazed Roast Ham also returns, building on an 82% repurchase intent in 2025. Also making a comeback are Walkers Pigs in Blankets and Roast Potatoes multipacks, which last appeared in 2023 and 2021 respectively, both with new non-HFSS recipes for 2026.
These innovations tap into shoppers’ appetite for something different at Christmas.
Rob Pothier, marketing director at PepsiCo, said: “Christmas is a huge opportunity for savoury snacking, with shoppers stocking up for every occasion, from family get-togethers and parties to nights in and the days between Christmas and New Year.
“In fact, 84% of shoppers say they stock up on snacks before the festivities begin [according to a Toluna poll], so retailers will want to make sure they have a strong mix of core favourites and seasonal flavours to give shoppers plenty of choice throughout the festive period.
“Our Christmas portfolio is designed to stand out in store and make it easy for shoppers to find what they need, whether that’s a familiar favourite or a seasonal flavour.”
The range will be supported by shopper marketing activity to drive visibility throughout the festive period.

items.title: Joe Marler and Tony Bellew challenge what it means to ‘man up’ in Jacamo’s AW26 campaign, ‘Jacamo vs Nature’
